name: Selank

b.x: A 62-patient Russian study set this peptide against the benzodiazepine medazepam in generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia and found comparable anxiolytic effects (Zozulya et al. 2008) [1]. A second study, in 60 patients, set it against phenazepam and reported anxiety relief that lasted a week after the last dose [2]. That level of clinical evidence puts Selank ahead of most research peptides. Selank (full sequence: Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic heptapeptide analog of tuftsin, developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences. Its mechanism hits multiple pathways at once. It inhibits enkephalinase, which extends the half-life of your body's own enkephalins. It modulates GABA receptor expression (confirmed at the gene level in) [3]. And it influences serotonin pathways and BDNF levels. The practical result is an anxiolytic that doesn't sedate you or dull your thinking. Users across dozens of Reddit threads on r/peptides and r/Nootropics describe it as "taking the edge off" while leaving focus intact. The most common community protocol is 250 to 500 mcg daily for 2 to 4 weeks, then cycling off for an equal period. Intranasal delivery has become the community's preferred route for its faster onset (15 to 30 min) and convenience. Two honest caveats: every published clinical trial originates from Russian academic institutions, with no independent Western replication to date. And the plasma half-life is very short (roughly 2 to 3 minutes IV), which means the mechanism behind its prolonged effect still isn't fully explained. The FDA removed Selank acetate from the Category 2 bulks list in September 2024; it remains research-only in the US.

Selank works through at least four distinct pathways, which is unusual for a seven-amino-acid peptide. The primary mechanism is enkephalinase inhibition. Enkephalins are your body's natural opioid peptides. Selank slows their degradation, extending their half-life and amplifying their calming effect on the nervous system. This produces anxiolysis without directly binding opioid receptors, avoiding the addiction and tolerance problems that plague benzodiazepines and opioids. At the gene expression level, Selank alters GABA receptor production. Volkova et al. [3] found 45 of 84 neurotransmission genes changed in rat frontal cortex an hour after a dose. GABA is the brain's primary inhibitory neurotransmitter; increasing its receptor density shifts the baseline toward calm. Serotonin modulation adds a third layer. Selank influences serotonergic activity, which contributes to mood stabilization. This is why concurrent use with SSRIs or SNRIs requires monitoring for additive serotonergic effects. The fourth pathway is BDNF regulation. Brain-derived neurotrophic factor drives synaptic plasticity, learning, and memory formation. In rats on chronic ethanol, a 7-day Selank course (0.3 mg/kg a day) prevented memory deficits and the ethanol-induced rise in hippocampal and frontal cortex BDNF (Kolik et al. 2019) [4]. Users report nootropic effects (verbal fluency, working memory) in weeks 2 to 3, later than the anxiolytic onset. As a tuftsin analog, Selank also retains immunomodulatory activity. Ershov et al. [5] documented immune function changes in patients with anxiety-asthenic disorders. This dual anxiolytic plus immune profile is what makes it distinctive.
Selank benefits center on anxiety reduction and cognitive support without the sedation or dependence risk that comes with conventional anxiolytics.
Matched the benzodiazepine medazepam for anxiety relief in a 62-patient Russian study, and added antiasthenic and stimulant effects (Zozulya et al. 2008) [1].
BDNF modulation may support learning and memory. Users consistently report improved verbal fluency and working memory by weeks 2 to 3 of a standard cycle.
No sedation or cognitive impairment at any studied dose. Community reports across dozens of Reddit threads describe maintained (or improved) focus during anxiolytic use.
Immunomodulatory activity as a tuftsin analog; Ershov et al. [5] confirmed immune function changes in anxiety-disorder patients receiving Selank.
Taken intranasally as a needle-free option. In BALB/c mice it worked by both nasal and injected routes (Vasil'eva et al. 2016) [6], and community reports describe a 15 to 30 minute onset.

Pairs well with Semax at a 2:1 ratio (400 mcg Selank to 200 mcg Semax intranasal) for combined anxiolytic and cognitive effects; the community figured this combination out before any formal trial tested it.

The main clinical evidence is a 62-patient Russian comparison with medazepam in generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia [1]. A 60-patient study compared it with phenazepam [2]. Neither abstract describes randomization or a placebo arm. Mechanisms include enkephalinase inhibition (prolonging enkephalin half-life), GABA receptor expression modulation [3], serotonin system effects, and BDNF modulation. All clinical research originates from Russian institutions: no Western RCTs have been conducted. FDA removed Selank acetate from Category 2 bulks list (September 27, 2024) but it remains research-only in the US.
Key Study
Zozulya et al. 2008 (PMID 18454096): 62 patients with GAD or neurasthenia, Selank (30) vs. medazepam (32), randomization not described. Selank vs. phenazepam in 60 patients: PMID 25176261.
Limitations

All clinical research from Russian academic institutions: no independent Western replication. No human intranasal bioavailability figure is published; PMID 29787664 is a mouse behaviour study. Half-life is very short (~2–10 min IV); mechanism of prolonged effect incompletely explained. No long-term human safety data beyond trial durations.

A 5 mg vial reconstituted with 2 mL of bacteriostatic water gives you 2,500 mcg/mL. At 250 mcg per dose, that's 0.10 mL, which is 10 units on a U-100 insulin syringe. At 500 mcg, you're pulling to the 20-unit mark. One vial gives you 10 doses at 500 mcg or 20 doses at 250 mcg. The thing most beginners miss with intranasal Selank: sniffing too hard drains the solution to your throat and bypasses mucosal absorption entirely. Tilt your head slightly forward, administer to one nostril, and give the gentlest sniff possible. Alternate nostrils per dose. Store reconstituted Selank at 2 to 8 degrees C and use within 28 days. Never freeze after reconstitution; ice crystals break the peptide apart. Lyophilized powder stores indefinitely at minus 20 degrees C before you add water. If a vial doesn't seem to work, check the COA purity (minimum 95% by HPLC) before assuming the peptide isn't for you. Product quality variation is the biggest variable in this space.
Selank Cycle 2–4 weeks on, 2–4 weeks off

Formal 14-day studies showed no measurable tolerance with daily Selank use. The 2–4 week on / 2–4 week off cycle is derived from the structure of Russian clinical trials, not from observed receptor desensitization data. No withdrawal syndrome has been documented in any published study. Cycling is a conservative default recommended by community consensus in the absence of long-term human safety data.

Alternative Routes
Intranasal spray
Split-dose required: 200–400 mcg per administration, 2–3x daily (vs. once-daily SubQ). Total daily dose roughly equivalent (400–900 mcg/day intranasal vs. 250–500 mcg/day SubQ).

No human bioavailability figure is published; in mice, selank worked by the nasal route (PMID 29787664). CNS delivery via olfactory pathway. Preferred by community for convenience and faster onset. Technique is critical: gentle sniff, alternate nostrils.
NA-Selank Amidate (intranasal)
Community reports roughly equivalent effect at 100–250 mcg/dose 1–2x daily: lower total daily dose vs. standard Selank. No peer-reviewed dose equivalence data exists.
N-acetyl + C-terminal amide modifications increase metabolic stability and claimed half-life extension enabling once-daily dosing. Treat as a distinct compound: start low.
Subcutaneous injection
250–500 mcg once daily. Slower onset (45–90 min) vs. intranasal but more consistent plasma exposure without split-dose requirement.
No SubQ-specific bioavailability data in humans. Community extrapolates from IV and intranasal data. Preferred by users wanting consistent once-daily dosing or those with nasal congestion issues.

SSRIs / SNRIs

Selank modulates serotonin via enkephalinase inhibition. Additive serotonergic activity possible. Monitor for serotonin excess signs (agitation, tremor, diaphoresis). Not absolutely contraindicated but requires monitoring.

The most important safety concern with Selank is its interaction profile, not the peptide itself. Selank modulates GABA receptor expression, serotonergic pathways, and enkephalin metabolism simultaneously. Combining it with benzodiazepines risks excessive CNS depression. Adding it to an SSRI or SNRI creates additive serotonergic activity; watch for agitation, tremor, and diaphoresis. If you're on immunosuppressive therapy (cyclosporine, tacrolimus, methotrexate), Selank's tuftsin-derived immunomodulatory effects may interfere with your intended immunosuppression. On its own, Selank looks mild in community reports, with little sedation. The medazepam study [1] and the phenazepam study [2] do not give adverse-event rates in their abstracts. No published study has measured dependence or withdrawal. What users actually report: the most common complaint is nasal stinging or irritation at higher intranasal doses (400 to 600 mcg per administration). Diluting with more bacteriostatic water or splitting the dose across both nostrils reduces this. Mild fatigue during the first one or two doses is occasionally mentioned but typically resolves quickly. Batch-to-batch inconsistency in unregulated research-grade products is the number one cause of "non-response" in community reports; that's a quality problem, not a pharmacological one. The effect is too subtle for acute panic. Selank is a background anxiolytic, not a rescue medication. If you're expecting benzodiazepine-level sedation on demand, you'll be disappointed. By design, the effect ceiling is lower. All published clinical data comes from Russian institutions. Total human trial exposure is limited to the study populations described above. No long-term safety data beyond trial durations (typically 2 to 4 weeks) exists. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are absolute contraindications due to insufficient safety data. Children under 18 have not been studied. Active autoimmune conditions may be affected by Selank's immunomodulatory properties. Practical stop signals: discontinue if you experience paradoxical anxiety increase, any hypersensitivity reaction (rash, itching), or signs of excessive serotonergic activity when combined with other medications. Consult a physician before combining Selank with any CNS-active medication.
Common Issues & Solutions

No effect after 1 week (SubQ): Verify the batch COA shows purity ≥95% by HPLC. Batch-to-batch inconsistency is the leading community-reported cause of non-response. Rule out a bad batch before escalating dose.
Nasal route not working: Administer with head slightly forward, gentle sniff only. Sniffing hard pushes solution to the throat (esophageal swallow = no absorption). Alternate nostrils per dose.

Semax stack causing irritability: Reduce Semax dose first (not Selank). Try 400 mcg Selank: 100 mcg Semax ratio before abandoning the stack. Selank dose can be increased to 500 mcg to further blunt Semax edge.
Anxiety returns after cycling off: Expected: this is a cycle-based anxiolytic, not a cure. Residual benefit lasts 1–2 weeks post-cycle. Restart after full off-period.

Nasal stinging at higher doses: Normal at 400–600 mcg intranasal per dose. Dilute with more BacWater (3 mL instead of 2 mL per 5 mg vial) or split across both nostrils to reduce mucosal irritant concentration per nostril.

Selank is classified as research-only in the United States. It is not FDA-approved for any medical condition. The FDA removed Selank acetate from the Category 2 bulk drug substances list on September 27, 2024 (nominations withdrawn), and it was not moved to Category 1. Its status remains pending review by the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC). Compounding via 503A pharmacies is not currently available through official channels. In Russia, Selank is an approved pharmaceutical product. The 0.15% nasal spray formulation has been registered and prescribed clinically. This approval does not extend to any other jurisdiction. Selank does not appear on the current World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) prohibited list, but athletes should verify against the most current list before use, as peptide classifications change periodically. All US research-grade Selank is sold for research purposes only and is not intended for human consumption. Peptide Schedule provides this information for educational and research reference purposes. This content does not constitute medical advice. Consult a licensed physician before using any peptide.

faqs.q: Does Selank cause tolerance? Do I need to cycle it?
faqs.a: Formal 14-day studies showed no measurable tolerance. But community consensus still follows the Russian clinical trial structure: 2-4 weeks on, 2-4 weeks off. No tolerance documented doesn't mean it can't happen with extended daily use. Cycling is the safe default.

faqs.q: Nasal spray or subcutaneous: which is better?
faqs.a: Depends on what you prefer. Nasal is the original pharmaceutical form: fast onset (15-30 min) but needs 2-3 doses daily. SubQ gives more consistent once-daily absorption and avoids the variable of nasal congestion. Neither is definitively superior.

faqs.q: How does Selank compare to Semax, and should I take both?
faqs.a: Selank leads with calming anxiolytic effects; Semax leads with cognitive drive. They're commonly stacked at a 2:1 ratio (e.g., 400 mcg Selank + 200 mcg Semax intranasal) because Selank smooths out Semax-induced irritability. Test each one separately first before combining.

faqs.q: How long does reconstituted Selank last?
faqs.a: At 2-8 degrees C in bacteriostatic water: about 28 days. Never freeze after reconstitution: ice crystals degrade the peptide. Lyophilized powder stores long-term at -20 degrees C.

faqs.q: Does Selank actually work for anxiety, or is it just placebo?
faqs.a: More clinical data than most nootropic peptides, all of it Russian. PMID 18454096 compared Selank (30 patients) with the benzodiazepine medazepam (32) in generalized anxiety disorder and neurasthenia. Anxiolytic effects were similar. The abstract does not describe randomization or a placebo arm. PMID 25176261 tested it against phenazepam in 60 patients and reported a clear anxiolytic effect that lasted a week after the last dose. The mechanism is well-characterized (enkephalinase inhibition, GABA/serotonin modulation). That said, effects are mild by benzodiazepine standards: by design.

faqs.q: What is the recommended Selank dosage?
faqs.a: Selank dosing varies by experience level. Beginners typically start at 250 mcg daily, moderate users at 500 mcg daily, and aggressive protocols use 750 mcg daily.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Selank?
faqs.a: The half-life of Selank is ~2-3 min (IV). This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.

summary: . Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is a synthetic analog of tuftsin, the immune peptide your body already makes. It calms anxiety through enkephalinase inhibition, GABA modulation, and serotonin regulation without sedation or cognitive fog. All published clinical data comes from Russian institutions; no Western replication exists yet.
